exams.title: HTML & Semantics — Topic Paper
exams.titleZh: HTML 与语义结构 · 专题卷
exams.description: Week 1 topic paper: HTML document structure, semantic landmarks and heading levels, links / images / paths, and lists, tables and code tags. Ten questions, three sub-questions each, with screenshot-style mockups.
exams.descriptionZh: Week 1 专题卷：HTML 文档骨架、语义地标与标题层级、链接 / 图片 / 路径，以及列表、表格与代码标签。共 10 道大题，每题 3 个子题，配套截图感 mockup。

questions.title: Gibberish menu
questions.contentMdx: `index.html` is Café Lumière's menu page. On phones the whole page looks tiny and some of the text shows as gibberish — for example "CrÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e" where the menu should read "Crème brûlée" — as `page.png` shows. Two important lines are missing from the page's `<head>`.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Look at `index.html`. Which two declarations are missing from the `<head>`, and what is each one responsible for?
subQuestions.answerMdx: The `<meta charset="utf-8">` declaration and the `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` declaration. The `charset` tells the browser which character encoding the bytes of the file use; the `viewport` tag tells a mobile browser to lay the page out at the device's own width instead of a wide default width.
subQuestions.markingMdx: 1 mark for naming both missing declarations (`charset` and `viewport`) and giving each one's job.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 观察 `index.html`。`<head>` 里缺了哪两行声明？各自负责什么？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 缺的是 `<meta charset="utf-8">` 和 `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`。`charset` 告诉浏览器这个文件的字节用的是什么字符编码；`viewport` 标签让移动端浏览器按设备自身宽度来排版，而不是用一个很宽的默认宽度。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh: 1 分：说出缺失的两条声明（`charset` 和 `viewport`），并分别说明各自作用。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why does the missing `charset` turn "Crème brûlée" into "CrÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e", and why does the missing `viewport` make the whole page look tiny and zoomed out on a phone?
subQuestions.answerMdx: The file is saved as UTF-8, so each accented character is stored as more than one byte (è is two bytes). With no `charset` declared, the browser has to guess an encoding — often a single-byte one such as windows-1252 — so it reads those two bytes as two separate characters and "è" becomes "Ã¨": the classic mojibake. The `viewport` tag works differently: without it a phone assumes a wide virtual page (about 980px) and then shrinks it to fit the screen, so all the text renders tiny; `width=device-width` makes the layout width equal the device width, so it maps 1:1.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining mojibake: without a declared charset the browser guesses an encoding and misreads the multi-byte UTF-8 characters.
1 mark for explaining the viewport: without it the phone uses a wide default page and scales it down, so everything looks tiny.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 为什么缺少 `charset` 会让 "Crème brûlée" 变成 "CrÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e"？又为什么缺少 `viewport` 会让整个页面在手机上显得很小、被缩小？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 文件是以 UTF-8 保存的，所以每个带重音的字符会占不止一个字节（è 是两个字节）。没有声明 `charset` 时，浏览器只能猜编码——常常猜成单字节编码（如 windows-1252），于是它把这两个字节读成两个独立的字符，"è" 就变成了 "Ã¨"：这就是典型的乱码。`viewport` 起作用的方式不同：没有它时，手机会假设一个很宽的虚拟页面（约 980px），再把它整体缩小到屏幕里，所以文字都变得很小；`width=device-width` 让布局宽度等于设备宽度，就能 1:1 映射。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：解释乱码——没有声明 charset 时浏览器靠猜编码，把多字节的 UTF-8 字符读错。
1 分：解释 viewport——没有它时手机按很宽的默认页面渲染再整体缩小，因此一切都显得很小。

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Rewrite the `<head>` of `index.html` so both problems are fixed, and say where these lines must sit.
subQuestions.answerMdx: Add both tags at the very top of `<head>`, with `charset` first so the browser knows the encoding before it reads any text: `<head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Café Lumière</title></head>`. The `charset` makes the browser decode the bytes correctly, so the accents render properly, and the `viewport` tag makes the phone lay the page out at the device width, so the text is no longer tiny. Both belong inside `<head>`, because they are metadata about the document rather than content shown on the page.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for adding `<meta charset="utf-8">` (ideally first in the head).
1 mark for adding the `viewport` meta with `width=device-width`, and for placing both lines inside `<head>`.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请重写 `index.html` 的 `<head>`，让两个问题都得到修复，并说明这两行应该放在哪里。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 把两行都放在 `<head>` 的最前面，且 `charset` 放第一行，这样浏览器在读取任何文本之前就知道编码：`<head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Café Lumière</title></head>`。`charset` 让浏览器正确解码字节，重音字符就能正常显示；`viewport` 让手机按设备宽度排版，文字不再变小。二者都应放在 `<head>` 内，因为它们是关于文档的元信息，而不是页面上展示的内容。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：加入 `<meta charset="utf-8">`（最好放在 head 最前面）。
1 分：加入带 `width=device-width` 的 `viewport` meta，并把两行都放在 `<head>` 内。

questions.title: A page made of divs
questions.contentMdx: `index.html` is the COMP6080 course homepage. Every region is a `<div>`, and the headings jump from `<h1>` straight to `<h3>`, as `outline.png` shows. A screen-reader user complains that they cannot jump straight to the navigation or to the main content.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Which two semantic landmarks are missing (and which `<div>`s should become them), and which heading level is skipped?
subQuestions.answerMdx: The navigation landmark `<nav>` and the main-content landmark `<main>` are missing: `<div class="menu">` should be a `<nav>` and `<div class="main">` should be a `<main>`. The heading levels also skip `<h2>` — the page goes from `<h1>` straight to `<h3>`.
subQuestions.markingMdx: 1 mark for naming both missing landmarks (`nav` and `main`) and identifying the skipped `<h2>`.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 缺了哪两个语义地标（对应的 `<div>` 应改成它们）？又跳过了哪一级标题？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 缺的是导航地标 `<nav>` 和主体内容地标 `<main>`：`<div class="menu">` 应改为 `<nav>`，`<div class="main">` 应改为 `<main>`。标题层级还跳过了 `<h2>`——页面从 `<h1>` 直接跳到 `<h3>`。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh: 1 分：说出缺失的两个地标（`nav` 和 `main`），并指出被跳过的 `<h2>`。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why does replacing those `<div>`s with landmarks matter for a screen-reader user, and how does the skipped `<h2>` make it worse?
subQuestions.answerMdx: A `<div>` carries no role, so it contributes nothing to the accessibility tree: a screen reader cannot present `<div class="menu">` as a "navigation" landmark or `<div class="main">` as "main", and the user has no shortcut to jump to either. `<nav>` and `<main>` create those landmarks, so the reader can list them and jump between them. The missing `<h2>` makes it worse because the heading outline now reads h1 → h3: that contradiction implies a section is missing, so someone navigating by heading level lands on a level that has no level above it in that branch.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining that a `<div>` has no landmark role, so screen readers cannot jump to navigation/main, whereas `nav`/`main` add those roles.
1 mark for explaining that the skipped `h2` breaks the heading outline (h1 → h3 implies a missing section).
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 把这些 `<div>` 换成地标，对读屏用户为什么重要？跳过的 `<h2>` 又为什么让情况更糟？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: `<div>` 不携带任何角色，对无障碍树没有任何贡献：读屏器无法把 `<div class="menu">` 呈现为 "navigation" 地标，也无法把 `<div class="main">` 呈现为 "main"，用户没有任何快捷方式可以跳到它们。`<nav>` 和 `<main>` 会创建这些地标，读屏器就能把它们列出来并在其间跳转。跳过的 `<h2>` 让情况更糟，是因为标题大纲现在读起来是 h1 → h3：这种矛盾暗示中间缺了一节，于是按标题层级导航的用户会落到一个在该分支上没有上一级的层级上。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 `<div>` 没有地标角色，读屏器无法跳到 navigation / main，而 `nav` / `main` 会补上这些角色。
1 分：说明跳过的 `h2` 破坏标题大纲（h1 → h3 暗示缺了一节）。

subQuestions.questionMdx: Rewrite the `<body>` using the right elements and fix the heading level, and explain why the class-based styling still works.

questions.title: Broken images and links
questions.contentMdx: `index.html` is a gallery at `gallery/index.html` that lists artworks. On the live site every image shows as a broken-image icon and each "Details" link lands on a 404, as `list.png` shows. The real image files sit under `assets/images/` at the site root.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The page uses ``. What path does the browser actually request, and why does the image fail to load?
subQuestions.answerMdx: The browser resolves the relative path against the page's own folder, so from `gallery/index.html` it requests `gallery/assets/images/art1.jpg`. That file does not exist — the images are under `assets/` at the site root, not inside `gallery/` — so the request 404s and the browser shows the broken-image placeholder.
subQuestions.markingMdx: 1 mark for stating the browser requests `gallery/assets/images/art1.jpg` (the relative path is joined onto the page's folder) and that the file is not there.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 页面里写的是 ``。浏览器实际请求的是什么路径？为什么图片加载失败？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 浏览器会把相对路径拼接到页面自身所在的目录上，所以从 `gallery/index.html` 出发，它请求的是 `gallery/assets/images/art1.jpg`。这个文件并不存在——图片在站点根目录的 `assets/` 下，而不是 `gallery/` 里——于是请求 404，浏览器显示图片损坏的占位图。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh: 1 分：说明浏览器实际请求的是 `gallery/assets/images/art1.jpg`（相对路径会拼到页面所在目录），而该文件并不存在。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why do the "Details" links fail for exactly the same reason, and why would the bug have been invisible if the page had stayed at the site root?
subQuestions.answerMdx: `<a href="detail.html">` is also relative, so from `gallery/index.html` the browser requests `gallery/detail.html`, which is not where the file lives — the same resolution rule that broke the images. Had the page been at the site root, its folder would be the root, so `assets/images/art1.jpg` and `detail.html` would both resolve to the correct files and everything would work. That is why the mistake is easy to miss: it only surfaces once the page is moved into a subfolder, because relative paths depend on the page's position.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining the links fail because relative paths resolve against the page's folder (`gallery/detail.html`).
1 mark for explaining the bug is position-dependent — it only appears after the page moves into a subfolder, so it is invisible at the root.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 为什么 "Details" 链接会因完全相同的原因失败？如果页面一直待在站点根目录，这个 bug 又为什么看不出来？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: `<a href="detail.html">` 同样是相对路径，所以从 `gallery/index.html` 出发，浏览器请求的是 `gallery/detail.html`，而文件并不在那里——和把图片弄坏的是同一条解析规则。如果页面待在站点根目录，它所在目录就是根目录，那么 `assets/images/art1.jpg` 和 `detail.html` 都会解析到正确的文件，一切正常。这正是这个错误容易被忽略的原因：只有当页面被移进子目录后它才暴露，因为相对路径依赖页面的位置。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明链接失败是因为相对路径会基于页面所在目录解析（`gallery/detail.html`）。
1 分：说明这是位置相关的 bug——页面移进子目录后才出现，在根目录下看不出来。

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Rewrite the image and link paths so they work from any folder, and explain why that form is more robust.
subQuestions.answerMdx: Use root-relative paths that start with `/`: `` and `Details`. A leading `/` makes the browser resolve the path from the site root, not from the current page's folder, so the same markup keeps working no matter how deep the page moves. That decouples the paths from the file's location, which is why root-relative paths are the safer default in a project with folders.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for rewriting both paths as root-relative (starting with `/`), e.g. `/assets/images/art1.jpg` and `/gallery/detail.html`.
1 mark for explaining that a leading `/` resolves from the site root, so the paths no longer depend on the page's folder.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请重写图片与链接的路径，让它们在任何目录下都能工作，并解释这种写法为什么更稳。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 改用以 `/` 开头的根路径：`` 和 `Details`。开头的 `/` 让浏览器从站点根目录解析路径，而不是从当前页面所在目录，所以无论页面移动多深，同一套 markup 都能继续工作。这样就把路径与文件位置解耦了，也是在带目录的项目里根路径更稳妥的原因。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：把两条路径都改成根路径（以 `/` 开头），例如 `/assets/images/art1.jpg` 和 `/gallery/detail.html`。
1 分：说明开头的 `/` 从站点根目录解析，因此路径不再依赖页面所在目录。

questions.title: A run-on results page
questions.contentMdx: `results.html` shows a marathon results page. The standings are built from `<div>` rows, the finishing steps are a single run-on `<div>`, and the code sample loses all its indentation, as `results.png` shows.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The finishing steps are one run-on `<div>`. Which element gives them ordered-list semantics, and what visual difference does it make by default?
subQuestions.answerMdx: An ordered list: `<ol>` with one `<li>` per step. By default the browser numbers the items (1., 2., 3.), which matches the fact that the steps have a fixed order — something a single `<div>` cannot express.
subQuestions.markingMdx: 1 mark for naming `<ol>` (with `<li>` items) and its default numbered, ordered appearance.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 完赛步骤现在是一个连成一串的 `<div>`。哪个元素能赋予它有序列表的语义？它默认会带来什么视觉差异？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 有序列表：`<ol>`，每一步一个 `<li>`。浏览器默认会给条目编号（1.、2.、3.），这与这些步骤有固定先后顺序相符——这是单独一个 `<div>` 无法表达的。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh: 1 分：说出 `<ol>`（配合 `<li>`），以及它默认带编号的有序外观。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why is a `<div>` grid the wrong choice for the standings, and why does the code sample lose its indentation?
subQuestions.answerMdx: A `<div>` grid only looks like a table: it carries no row/column semantics, so a screen reader cannot announce "column Race time, row 2" or tie a cell back to its header, and there is nothing programmatic for the browser's reading or printing to use. A real `<table>` with `<thead>` and `<th>` provides that structure. The code sample loses its indentation because HTML collapses any run of spaces, tabs and newlines into a single space; without a `<pre>` element to preserve the original whitespace, the multi-line, indented code is flattened onto one line.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining that div rows have no table semantics, so headers and cells are not programmatically linked (a real `table`/`thead`/`th` is needed).
1 mark for explaining that HTML collapses runs of whitespace and newlines, which is why the indentation disappears.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 为什么用 `<div>` 网格来做排名是错误的选择？代码示例又为什么会丢失缩进？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: `<div>` 网格只是看起来像表格：它不携带任何行/列语义，所以读屏器无法报出 "column Race time, row 2"，也无法把单元格与其表头关联，浏览器在朗读或打印时也没有可用的结构化信息。真正的 `<table>` 配合 `<thead>` 和 `<th>` 才能提供这种结构。代码示例丢失缩进，是因为 HTML 会把任意连续的空白、制表符和换行都折叠成一个空格；没有 `<pre>` 元素来保留原始空白，这段多行、带缩进的代码就会被压平到一行。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 div 行没有表格语义，表头与单元格没有程序化的关联（需要真正的 `table`/`thead`/`th`）。
1 分：说明 HTML 会折叠连续的空白与换行，因此缩进消失。

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Rewrite the three areas — steps, standings and code — with the correct elements, and explain why each fix works.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for using `<ol>`/`<li>` for the steps and `<table>`/`<thead>`/`<th>` (with `<tbody>`/`<td>`) for the standings.
1 mark for using `<pre><code>` for the code sample and explaining that `pre` preserves whitespace.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请用正确的元素重写这三块——步骤、排名、代码——并解释每个改法为什么有效。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：用 `<ol>`/`<li>` 表达步骤，用 `<table>`/`<thead>`/`<th>`（配合 `<tbody>`/`<td>`）表达排名。
1 分：用 `<pre><code>` 表达代码示例，并说明 `pre` 会保留空白。

questions.title: Headings chosen by size
questions.contentMdx: `guide.html` is a documentation page. To make the page title smaller than the browser's default `<h1>`, the author used `<h2>`, and to get small bold section labels they used `<h4>` for every section. The page never uses `<h1>` and jumps from `<h2>` straight to `<h4>`, as `sizes.png` shows.
questions.contentMdxZh: `guide.html` 是一个文档页。为了让页面标题比浏览器默认的 `<h1>` 小一些，作者用了 `<h2>`；为了得到小而粗的章节标签，每个章节都用了 `<h4>`。整页没有 `<h1>`，而且从 `<h2>` 直接跳到 `<h4>`，如 `sizes.png` 所示。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: What two problems does this create in the document's heading structure?
subQuestions.answerMdx: The top-level heading is `<h2>` instead of `<h1>`, so the page has no level-1 heading at all; and the levels skip — the outline goes from `<h2>` straight to `<h4>` with no `<h3>` in between.
subQuestions.markingMdx: 1 mark for naming both problems: no `<h1>` at the top, and a skipped level (`h2` → `h4`, no `h3`).
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 这样做让文档的标题结构出现了哪两个问题？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 最顶层标题是 `<h2>` 而不是 `<h1>`，所以整页根本没有一级标题；而且层级出现跳级——大纲从 `<h2>` 直接到 `<h4>`，中间没有 `<h3>`。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh: 1 分：说清两个问题——最顶层没有 `<h1>`，以及出现跳级（`h2` → `h4`，缺 `h3`）。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why does this break navigation for a screen-reader user, and why is choosing a heading by the text size it produces the wrong reason?
subQuestions.answerMdx: Heading levels build a tree that screen readers use to summarise and navigate the page: a user can list all headings or jump to the next heading of a given level. With no `<h1>`, a user who jumps to level 1 lands on nothing, and with `<h2>` → `<h4>` the outline claims two deeper levels exist that are missing, so the tree is inconsistent and the user cannot tell which sections are peers of which. Choosing a level by the font size it renders is wrong because the element is meant to express structure, not appearance — the size is a styling decision that belongs in CSS. Picking `<h4>` for a small label means the level no longer reflects where that section sits in the hierarchy.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining that heading levels form the outline tree a screen reader navigates (no `h1` and skipped levels make it inconsistent/unusable).
1 mark for explaining that a heading level conveys structure, not size, so the visual size should come from CSS instead.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 这为什么会破坏读屏用户的导航？又为什么「按标题渲染出来的字号大小来选标题级别」是错误理由？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 标题层级构成一棵树，读屏器用它来概述和导航页面：用户可以列出所有标题，或跳到某一层级的下一个标题。没有 `<h1>` 时，跳到一级标题的用户会落空；而 `<h2>` → `<h4>` 让大纲声称存在两个更深的层级却缺失，于是这棵树自相矛盾，用户无法判断哪些章节是同级。按渲染出的字号来选级别之所以错误，是因为元素本应表达结构而非外观——字号是样式决定，属于 CSS。为了得到一个小的标签而选用 `<h4>`，会让该级别不再反映这一节在层级中的位置。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明标题层级构成读屏器导航所依赖的大纲树（缺 h1、跳级都会让它矛盾/不可用）。
1 分：说明标题级别表达的是结构而非字号，视觉大小应由 CSS 负责。

questions.title: Sections with no names
questions.contentMdx: `landing.html` is a product landing page. The main content is already wrapped in `<main>`, but inside it every block is a `<section>` whose title is a plain `<div class="title">`, so no section actually contains a heading. A strip of advertising is also a `<section>`, sitting between the features and the sign-up form, as `regions.png` shows.
questions.contentMdxZh: `landing.html` 是一个产品落地页。主内容已经用 `<main>` 包好了，但里面每个区块都是 `<section>`，而它们的标题只是普通的 `<div class="title">`，所以没有任何 section 真正包含标题。一条广告条也是 `<section>`，夹在功能介绍和注册表单之间，如 `regions.png` 所示。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: What is wrong with the `<section>` blocks, and which block uses the wrong element for its role?
subQuestions.answerMdx: None of the `<section>` blocks contains a heading — their titles are plain `<div>`s — so the sections have no accessible name. The advertising strip is not part of the page's main content, so it should be an `<aside>` (complementary content), not a `<section>`.
subQuestions.markingMdx: 1 mark for noting that the sections have no heading (so no name), and that the ad strip should be `<aside>`.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 这些 `<section>` 区块有什么问题？哪个区块用错了元素？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 没有任何一个 `<section>` 里有标题——它们的标题都是普通的 `<div>`——所以这些 section 没有可访问名称。广告条并不属于页面的主内容，因此它应该是 `<aside>`（补充性内容），而不是 `<section>`。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh: 1 分：指出这些 section 没有标题（因此没有名称），且广告条应是 `<aside>`。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why does a `<section>` without a heading cause a problem for assistive technology, and why does labelling the ad as `<aside>` matter?
subQuestions.answerMdx: A `<section>` only becomes a meaningful, navigable region when it has an accessible name, and that name comes from a heading (or an `aria-label`). With only a `<div class="title">` inside, the section is just a generic container: screen-reader users get no name to list or jump to, so region navigation cannot distinguish "Features" from "Sign up". Making the ad an `<aside>` matters because it marks that content as complementary rather than primary: assistive tech can group and skip it, and the reading order makes clear it is not the page's main message. Incorrectly marking the ad as a `<section>` blurs it into the page's structural content.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining that a section needs a heading (or `aria-label`) to get an accessible name, otherwise region navigation cannot identify it.
1 mark for explaining that `<aside>` marks complementary content so it can be grouped/skipped as not-primary.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 为什么没有标题的 `<section>` 会给辅助技术带来问题？把广告标成 `<aside>` 又为什么重要？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: `<section>` 只有在拥有可访问名称时才会成为一个有意义、可导航的区域，而这个名称来自标题（或 `aria-label`）。如果里面只有一个 `<div class="title">`，这个 section 就只是个通用容器：读屏用户拿不到名字去列出或跳转，区域导航也就无法区分 "Features" 和 "Sign up"。把广告做成 `<aside>` 很重要，因为它把这部分内容标记为补充性而非主体：辅助技术可以对其分组、跳过，阅读顺序也表明它不是页面的主旨。把广告错标成 `<section>` 会让它混进页面的结构内容里。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 section 需要一个标题（或 aria-label）才能获得可访问名称，否则区域导航无法识别它。
1 分：说明 `<aside>` 标记补充性内容，可被分组/跳过，不当作主体。

questions.title: A link that acts, a button that navigates
questions.titleZh: 链接装成动作、按钮装成导航
questions.contentMdx: `app.html` is a task app. The "Save draft" action is written as `Save draft`, and the "Docs" navigation item is written as ``, as `ui.png` shows.
questions.contentMdxZh: `app.html` 是一个任务应用。"Save draft" 这个动作被写成 `Save draft`，而 "Docs" 这个导航项被写成 ``，如 `ui.png` 所示。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Which element should each of these two be, and why are they swapped?
subQuestions.answerMdx: "Save draft" performs an action, so it should be a `<button>`; "Docs" navigates to a page, so it should be an `<a href="/docs">`. They are swapped: the action is a link and the navigation is a button.
subQuestions.markingMdx: 1 mark for stating the action should be a `<button>` and the navigation should be an `<a href>`.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 这两处分别该用什么元素？为什么说它们被弄反了？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: "Save draft" 执行的是动作，应该是 `<button>`；"Docs" 是跳转到某个页面，应该是 `<a href="/docs">`。它们是反的：动作被做成了链接，导航被做成了按钮。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh: 1 分：说明动作应是 `<button>`、导航应是 `<a href>`。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why does `Save draft` behave badly, and what do you lose by making the navigation a `
subQuestions.answerMdx: A link is announced as a link and is expected to take the user somewhere; with `href="#"` it points at the top of the current page, so activating "Save draft" just jumps the view to the top and saves nothing, while assistive tech still calls it a link. It also gets link affordances it should not have (open in new tab, copy link address). Making "Docs" a `<button>` loses the browser's link behaviour: it cannot be opened in a new tab, copied, bookmarked or long-pressed, and it is announced as a button, so users expect an in-page action rather than navigation. A `<button onclick=...>` also breaks if JavaScript fails, whereas a real link works on its own.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining that `href="#"` makes the action jump to the page top and is misleadingly announced as a link.
1 mark for explaining that a `<button>` for navigation loses open-in-new-tab / copy / bookmark behaviour and is announced as a button.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: `Save draft` 为什么表现很糟？把导航做成 `
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 链接会被播报为链接，用户预期它会把人带到某处；而 `href="#"` 指向当前页面顶部，于是激活 "Save draft" 只会让视图跳到顶部、什么都没保存，辅助技术却仍把它叫链接。它还带上了本不该有的链接能力（新标签页打开、复制链接地址）。把 "Docs" 做成 `<button>` 则丢掉了浏览器的链接行为：无法新标签页打开、无法复制、无法收藏或长按，而且它被播报为按钮，用户会预期这是页内动作而非跳转。`<button onclick=...>` 在 JavaScript 失效时也会坏掉，而真正的链接本身就能工作。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 `href="#"` 让动作跳到页面顶部，且被误导性地播报为链接。
1 分：说明用 `<button>` 做导航会失去新标签页打开/复制/收藏等行为，并被播报为按钮。

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Rewrite both so the element matches the job, and explain why the fix works.
subQuestions.answerMdx: Action: `` — a button is announced as a button, is focusable and keyboard-operable by default, and performs its action without moving the page. Navigation: `Docs` — a real link works without JavaScript, can be opened in a new tab and copied, and is announced as a link. Swapping them back means each control now exposes the role, keyboard behaviour and browser affordances that match what it actually does.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for rewriting the action as `<button>` (ideally `type="button"`) and the navigation as `<a href="/docs">`.
1 mark for explaining that the correct element brings the matching role, keyboard behaviour and browser affordances.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请重写这两处，让元素与它的职责相符，并解释改法为什么有效。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 动作：``——按钮被播报为按钮，默认可聚焦、可用键盘操作，并且执行动作时不移动页面。导航：`Docs`——真正的链接不依赖 JavaScript 即可工作，可以新标签页打开、可以复制，并被播报为链接。把它们换回来，意味着每个控件现在都暴露了与其实际职责相匹配的角色、键盘行为和浏览器能力。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：把动作重写为 `<button>`（最好带 `type="button"`），把导航重写为 `<a href="/docs">`。
1 分：说明正确的元素带来匹配的角色、键盘行为和浏览器能力。

questions.title: A fake button and a missing language
questions.contentMdx:
`index.html` has an `` element with no `lang` attribute, and the "Buy" control is a `
Buy
` that cannot be focused or activated by keyboard, as `a11y.png` shows.
questions.contentMdxZh:
`index.html` 的 `` 没有 `lang` 属性，而 "Buy" 控件是一个 `
Buy
`，无法被键盘聚焦或激活，如 `a11y.png` 所示。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: What is missing from the `<html>` element, and what is wrong with the "Buy" control?
subQuestions.answerMdx: The `<html>` element is missing the `lang` attribute, so the page has no declared language. The "Buy" control is a `<div>` with `role="button"`, a fake button — it is not a real `<button>` element.
subQuestions.markingMdx: 1 mark for naming the missing `lang` attribute on `<html>` and identifying the `<div role="button">` as a fake button.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: `<html>` 元素缺了什么？"Buy" 这个控件又有什么问题？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: `<html>` 元素缺了 `lang` 属性，页面没有声明语言。"Buy" 控件是一个带 `role="button"` 的 `<div>`，是个假按钮——它不是真正的 `<button>` 元素。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh: 1 分：说出 `<html>` 缺少 `lang` 属性，并指出 `<div role="button">` 是假按钮。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why does the missing `lang` matter to assistive technology, and why isn't adding `role="button"` to a `<div>` enough?
subQuestions.answerMdx: Screen readers use the document's language to choose the correct pronunciation rules, and browsers use it for spell-checking and translation; with no `lang`, those tools guess and may read English with the wrong accent or offer the wrong dictionary. For the control, `role="button"` only changes how the element is announced (as a button) — it does not add any of a button's behaviour. A `<div>` is not focusable and has no keyboard activation, so a keyboard user cannot Tab to "Buy" or press Enter/Space to activate it; ARIA changes the name and role, not the behaviour. That is why the rule is "no ARIA is better than bad ARIA": use the native element, which gives the role and the behaviour together.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining that `lang` drives screen-reader pronunciation and spell-check/translation, so guessing the language mispronounces or mistranslates.
1 mark for explaining that `role="button"` only changes the announced role and adds no focus or keyboard activation, so a keyboard user cannot use the fake button.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 缺失 `lang` 为什么对辅助技术有影响？为什么给 `<div>` 加 `role="button"` 还不够？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 读屏器用文档语言选择正确的发音规则，浏览器也用它做拼写检查和翻译；没有 `lang` 时，这些工具只能猜，可能用错误口音朗读英文或给出错误的词典。对控件而言，`role="button"` 只改变元素被播报的方式（被读成按钮）——它不会补上按钮的任何行为。`<div>` 不可聚焦、也没有键盘激活方式，所以键盘用户无法 Tab 到 "Buy"，也无法按 Enter/Space 激活它；ARIA 改变的是名称和角色，不是行为。这就是那条规则的原因："没有 ARIA 好过糟糕的 ARIA"——应使用原生元素，它会同时给出角色和行为。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 `lang` 决定读屏发音、拼写检查与翻译，猜语言会导致读错或译错。
1 分：说明 `role="button"` 只改变被播报的角色，不提供聚焦或键盘激活，键盘用户无法使用这个假按钮。

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Fix the document so the language is declared and the control is a real button, and explain why this is better than patching the `<div>`.
subQuestions.answerMdx: Add the language to the root element — `<html lang="en">` — so screen readers, spell-checkers and translators no longer have to guess. Replace the fake button with the native element: `<button type="button" class="btn">Buy</button>`. A real `<button>` is focusable and keyboard-operable and is announced as a button with no ARIA needed, so the role and the behaviour arrive together. Patching the `<div>` instead would mean adding `tabindex="0"` and a keydown handler to reproduce what the browser already does for free, which is more code and more ways to get it wrong.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for adding `lang` to `<html>` (e.g. `<html lang="en">`).
1 mark for replacing the `<div role="button">` with a real `<button>`, explaining that the native element provides role and keyboard behaviour together.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请修复文档，声明语言并把控件改成真正的按钮，并解释这为什么比给 `<div>` 打补丁更好。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 在根元素上声明语言——`<html lang="en">`——这样读屏器、拼写检查和翻译就不必再猜。把假按钮换成原生元素：`<button type="button" class="btn">Buy</button>`。真正的 `<button>` 可聚焦、可键盘操作，并被播报为按钮、无需任何 ARIA，因此角色和行为一起到位。若改为给 `<div>` 打补丁，就要加 `tabindex="0"` 和一个 keydown 处理程序，去复现浏览器本就免费提供的东西，代码更多、也更容易出错。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：给 `<html>` 加上 `lang`（如 `<html lang="en">`）。
1 分：把 `<div role="button">` 换成真正的 `<button>`，并说明原生元素同时提供角色与键盘行为。
